transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this final-lock meeting started. We've got Night Signal opening to ticketed visitors this Friday, and I need to hear from each of you before I can make my call. Let's go in order — technical lead, then accessibility lead, then labor lead. Please give me your standard operating reports on the public-opening package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before I give my standard report, I need to disclose a critical finding from this morning. I completed the fire-marshal egress walkthrough today, and the result is that the installation may admit at most 72 visitors at once — not 96 as the draft plan assumes — and visitors must be routed one-way clockwise through the east exit, not two-way circulation. I have not yet entered the signed walkthrough result into the production lock memo, but this directly affects the public-opening package we're reviewing.

transcript.text: I need to report my accessibility findings for the standard operating report. I tested the artist's approved accessible build with the artist's interface technician and confirmed that each session requires a 12-minute seated orientation plus four captioned control tablets reserved for visitors who need them. The artist sent the final accessibility specification directly to me yesterday, and I have not yet attached it to the lock memo.

transcript.text: I need to give my labor lead report now. Last night I reviewed the depot crew's applicable union agreement with the labor office, and I can confirm that the installation's three visitor zones require two qualified floor attendants per zone — that means exactly six attendants during every public session. The draft plan currently assumes only four floor attendants, which does not meet the union requirement. I have not yet updated the staffing sheet to reflect this, but this directly affects the public-opening package.
